passage: Just before the maths test, a friend whispered to Kalyani, "Let me copy yours." She said no, and promised to go through the method once school ended, and they stayed friends. Noor was asked the same thing and worked it out in his head. Copying would give a mark but no learning, and the next chapter would leave him lost, so helping his friend copy was not really helping. Aman showed his answers because he feared his friend would stop talking to him. Afterwards he worried all evening, since the teacher might blame both of them, and the worry only grew. Kabir said no twice. Then he heard that his friend planned to bring a small chit into the exam. He went to the teacher privately after school and told them, because stopping something bigger seemed worth it. The teacher thanked him, said the friend would be spoken to that same day, and asked Kabir not to worry.

qa.q: Whom did the friend whisper to before the maths test?
How does Aman's choice differ from Kalyani's, and what did each feel afterwards?
qa.a: Aman gave in to keep his friend and worried afterwards. Kalyani said no and offered help after class, and they stayed friends.

qa.q: What was Aman feeling that evening, and why?
qa.a: Aman was anxious and afraid, because the teacher might blame both of them and his fear kept growing.

qa.q: What could Aman do to put things right?
qa.a: He could tell his friend he was wrong to share the answers, and talk to the teacher or a parent about what happened. Offering to explain the method instead would be a better way to help.

grounding: Children answer a friend's wish to copy by refusing kindly, thinking about what a test is for, giving in from fear, and telling the teacher when it will not stop.
